name: Venetic

ancestors.notes: Indo-European; exact subgroup unresolved (Wikipedia: Venetic language; Pellegrini & Prosdocimi 1967).
Proposed but disputed 'Italo-Celtic-Venetic' contact/affiliation (e.g. a 2016 proposal grouping Venetic with Italic); treated as unproven contact, not a genetic parent.

notes: Skeleton. Extinct Indo-European language of ancient Veneto/Friuli and parts of Slovenia (6th-1st c. BCE), ~300 short inscriptions, transmitted in the Venetic alphabet (a Northern Italic script related to Etruscan, mostly written right-to-left) and, in the latest inscriptions (150-50 BCE), in the Latin alphabet as Latin loanwords flooded in. Scored here in the conventional epigraphic Latin transliteration used in the standard grammar (Pellegrini & Prosdocimi 1967): five vowels ⟨a e i o u⟩; the digraph ⟨vh⟩ (replacing the earlier Etruscan 8-shaped sign) for /f/, later replaced by ⟨h⟩ in some regions once [h] was lost — both are attested spellings and are kept distinct; ⟨ś⟩ a palatal fricative or dental affricate; the Greek-derived transliteration letters ⟨θ φ χ⟩ for aspirated stops, following the same convention used for Etruscan (ett.json). Exact IE subgrouping (independent branch vs. Italic vs. an Italo-Celtic-Venetic node) is unresolved in the literature; only the safe IE parent is asserted here.
